extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, scientists, and students of scientific method (readers of Bacon)
extracted.subtask_description: Method for discovering the 'form' (law) of a natural quality (example: heat) by collecting instances, excluding contrary natures, and then cautiously forming and testing affirmative hypotheses (the 'first vintage'). Emphasises tables of instances, solitary/coruscating cases, and experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Degrees / Comparative Instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and arrange instances that show varying degrees of the quality under investigation (e.g., degrees of heat: potential heat, barely perceptible warmth, animal heat, flame, ignited metals, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use many concrete examples showing gradations (points 1–41 in the Table of Degrees). Pay attention to potential vs. actual manifestations, comparative lists (which substances warm more readily), and sensory relativity (lukewarm water may seem hot or cold depending on the hand). Record suggestions and 'let the experiment be tried' notes attached to instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive Table (Rejection of Natures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble instances that demonstrate what the candidate 'natures' are not — i.e., list reasons to reject proposed causes or characteristics for the phenomenon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each contradictory instance (even a single one) can destroy a hypothesis. The Exclusive Table lists instances that exclude terrestrial/celestial origin, rarity, flame/light, mixing of substances, absolute expansion, destructive nature, etc., with numbered exclusions (examples 1–14). Use these to prune hypotheses before affirmative claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceed by Negatives First, Then Affirmatives (Methodological Caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not immediately assert an affirmative form; first reject incompatible natures and restrict possibilities by negatives, then proceed to affirmative interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mind is inclined to form premature theories; instead perform exclusion via the tables and only then attempt the 'first vintage' (a cautious affirmative). Avoid vague, ill-defined candidate natures; prefer elimination before positive definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Vintage / Liberty of the Understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: After collecting review and exclusion tables, attempt a provisional affirmative interpretation (a tentative form) guided by the collected instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat this 'first vintage' as provisional and constrained by instances. Select conspicuous ('coruscating') examples where the form is clearer; propose a working form/hypothesis (e.g., 'heat is expansive motion restrained...') and then test and refine it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Defined as Law Present in Every Instance
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the form (true nature) of a quality as that law or regulation of action which is inherent in each individual instance where the quality occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form must be found in all true instances; it is not an abstract metaphysical essence nor merely a compound concrete form. When rejecting candidate features, test whether they are present in every instance of the quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Coruscations / Conspicuous Instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer instances in which the form is least restrained by other natures — these reveal the form most clearly (called coruscations or conspicuous instances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek examples where interfering factors are minimal so the target nature stands out; these accelerate correct interpretation and make affirmative hypotheses clearer and more reliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solitary (Prerogative) Instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ solitary instances: subjects that share nothing with ordinary examples except the quality in question, or subjects resembling others except for the quality — these are especially powerful for exclusion and confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: prisms, crystalline gems, dews for color studies. A few solitary instances can be as decisive as many ordinary ones for rejecting spurious commonalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any Single Contradictory Instance Invalidates a Hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: A single well-attested contradictory instance suffices to destroy a proposed hypothesis about the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Exclusive Table: do not rely on seemingly general patterns if even one instance shows the candidate nature absent (or present where it shouldn't be).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish Form from Transitive/Communicative Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate the intrinsic form (the law constituting the quality) from the transitive or communicative phenomena (e.g., 'heating' as the communication of heat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., the ability of a hot body to warm another depends on assimilation/multiplication (a different, more profound nature). Do not confuse modes of transmission with the form itself when defining a nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental Testing and 'Let the Experiment Be Tried'
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify instances and exclusions by directed experiments (e.g., thermometers/weather-glasses, burning-glasses, tongs in fire, compression of tinder, heating with bellows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the text says 'Let the experiment be tried' attach concrete tests: use burning-glasses at varying distances, thermometer constructions, placing tongs/poker vertically/sloping in fire, compressing burning tinder, etc. Experiments should probe suggested distinctions and differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operative/Experimental Definition (Capable of Being Invoked)
rubrics_metrics.description: An operative definition of the form should tell what to do experimentally: if one can excite the proposed defining motion/condition in any susceptible body and thereby produce the quality, the definition is operational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., Bacon's operative definition of heat: excite a dilating/expansive motion which is partially restrained in small particles; doing so should produce heat regardless of substance. Practical manipulability is required for testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check Specific Differences as Limits on a Genus
rubrics_metrics.description: When identifying a form as a genus (e.g., motion), test for specific differences that delimit it. For heat Bacon lists four such differences that a satisfactory account must satisfy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the enumerated differences as a checklist to evaluate candidate explanations (see next four metric entries for Bacon's differences for heat).

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference I — Heat as Expansive Motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether the candidate form shows expansive motion: the body strives to dilate and occupy more space (seen in flame, boiling liquids, evaporation, expansion of air).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for swelling, boiling, vaporization, exudation, and expansion in thermometers. Rejection example: if a candidate implies rarity or celestial nature but does not account for expansion, reject it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference II — Upward Tendency of Heat's Expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the expansive motion tends outward and also upward (heat tends to rise; flame and hot vapors rise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical tests: place heated rods/poker vertical vs sloping and compare burning of the hand; distillation 'per descensum' observation; test whether cold contracts downward by analogous experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference III — Particle-scale, Non-uniform Expansive Motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the motion is not a uniform bulk expansion but an alternating motion of small particles, producing agitation and local effects (flame, boiling, burning by minute pores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish uniform dilation (which may be unperceived as heat) from alternating particle motion (which produces perceptible heat). Observe burning intensity at flame edges vs centre, action on small pores, and behaviour under confinement/compression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference IV — Rapidity / Non-sluggishness of the Motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the motion is rapid and energetic (not slow like time's effects), acting on particles of tolerable, not infinitesimal, size — rapid penetration/irritation produces perceived heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare slow chemical/temporal processes (which may produce similar effects without heat sensation) to violent/rapid processes like iron dissolution or brisk combustion; note differences in felt heat and violence of reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Three-stage Method: Review, Exclusion, Affirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the staged procedure: (1) collect tables of review (instances), (2) construct exclusive tables to reject candidate natures, (3) attempt the first vintage (provisional affirmative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each stage informs the next; repetition and iteration are expected. Do not assume the exclusive table is perfect initially; refine with further instances and experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer Experimental Corroboration Over Mere Report or Tradition
rubrics_metrics.description: Where traditions or reports exist, flag their doubtful credit and prefer experiment and confirmed instances; when historical examples are sparse use 'let the experiment be tried.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author inserts notes when credit is doubtful and repeatedly insists on experimental proof for many claimed effects (e.g., alleged human warmth melting butter, fire by subterranean causes, degree ordering of planets' heat).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remember Senses are Relative; Account for Sensory Relativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that sensible effects (e.g., warm/cold to touch) are relative to the observer's state; objective measurement and comparative instances are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: lukewarm water feels hot to a cold hand, cold to a warm hand; thermometric constructions (air/thermometer) recommended to capture subtle variations beyond human touch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Prerogative Helps: Supports, Corrections, Varying Investigation, Limits, Practical Application, Preparations, Axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond the basic tables, apply further methodological aids: identify prerogative instances, supports for induction, correction mechanisms, vary the investigation by subject, order research objectives, set limits, apply findings practically, prepare investigations, and set ascending/descending axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these as higher-level methodological modules to organise and refine inquiry; they are to be applied according to the nature and complexity of the subject under study.
